title: One solid, two ways to slice it: washers, shells and a cross-section, each with its error printed
summary: The Revolve workspace builds a solid from a region and shows its volume as a sum of thin pieces. The same solid with a hole is cut into washers (perpendicular to the axis) and into cylindrical shells (parallel to it); a Manim render shows the limit; a Steinmetz solid shows what a clever cross-section can do.

media.alt: Screenshot of the Revolve workspace. Left, a control panel with the curve y equals 4 minus (x minus 2) squared on x from 1 to 3 revolved about the vertical line x equals 0, 128 slices. Centre, the plane region as a green dome with an orange strip highlighted. Right, a teal solid of revolution with a hole, one orange washer pulled out and shown as a flat ring. A readout lists the slice thickness, the Riemann sum 92.16133, the exact value 92.15338 and the error 0.0079.

read_the_figure.question: What is the volume, as a sum of thin pieces, and how close is the sum to the exact value for this number of pieces?
read_the_figure.axes: Left graph: x and y of the plane region. Right: the 3D solid. Panel: the readout lines (number of slices, thickness, highlighted slice volume, sum, exact value, error, whether there is a hole).
look_at: The orange strip in the plane region is one slice; the orange ring or the curved sheet in 3D is the same slice after revolving. Match them.
Washers (first screenshot): each slice is a ring with outer radius r_out and inner radius r_in; the readout shows its volume as pi (r_out squared minus r_in squared) times thickness.
Shells (second screenshot): each slice is a thin cylinder of radius rho, height h and thickness d rho; the readout shows 2 pi rho h d rho and a smaller error (5.11e-4).
The Manim frame shows the formula and the limit: with 96 pieces the sum is 92.1543, exact 92.1534, error 9.1e-04.
The Steinmetz picture shows two cylinders crossing at right angles; the region common to both is the solid, cut by a plane to show its square cross-section.
Always check that the same exact value (92.15338) appears in both methods: that is the consistency test.
read_the_figure.proves: Washers and shells are two decompositions of one volume and must give the same exact answer; the printed error shows how fast the sum converges as slices thin. The Steinmetz picture shows a case where a different slicing makes the integral easy.
if_wrong: Different exact values from washers and shells: a wrong radius or the wrong axis in one formula.
An error that does not shrink when the slices are doubled: the formula has a systematic mistake.
A hole ignored: the inner radius is missing and the volume is too large.
A shell formula with the wrong radius (distance from the axis, not x).
must_check: That the axis of revolution is stated (x = 0 here).
That the method (washers or shells) matches the slice drawn.
That the exact value and the sum are both printed with the error.
That the number of slices is visible.

terms.meaning: A flat ring: a thin slice perpendicular to the axis with an outer and an inner radius.
A thin tube around the axis with radius rho, height h and thickness d rho.
A sum of piece volumes that tends to the integral as the pieces become thin.
The volume of a solid of revolution is the area of the region times the distance travelled by its centroid.
The region common to two perpendicular cylinders of equal radius.

remember: Washers: integrate pi (R squared minus r squared) along the axis. Shells: integrate 2 pi rho h across the axis.
The error of a midpoint Riemann sum falls roughly as 1 over n squared; of a left sum as 1 over n.
Both methods must agree on the exact value.
Pappus gives a one-line check: area times 2 pi times the centroid distance.
A good slicing makes cross-sections simple shapes.

steps.title: Shell integral for the solid in the first two screenshots
steps.note: Radius is the distance from the axis x = 0, height is the curve (the bottom is y = 0).

steps.title: Evaluate it
steps.note: The odd terms integrate to zero by symmetry. The value matches the exact number printed in the panel (92.15338).

steps.title: Pappus check
steps.note: The region is symmetric about x = 2 so its centroid is at x = 2; same answer in one line.

steps.title: Steinmetz volume by square cross-sections
steps.note: Cut the common region by planes perpendicular to the cylinder axes: every cross-section is a square of side 2 sqrt(r^2 - z^2).

worked.title: The shell method in numbers
worked.problem: With 128 slices on [1, 3], the thickness is 2/128. Estimate the volume with midpoints of one slice at x = 2 (height 4): compute the volume of that shell.

solution.text: The panel's highlighted shell reads 0.7885, close (its x is not exactly 2).

worked.answer: About 0.79 for one shell; 128 such shells sum to 92.15.

analyze.q: Why is the error printed for washers (0.0079) larger than for shells (5e-4) in these screenshots?
Why is the exact value the same in both screenshots?

evaluate.q: A student writes the shell radius as x - 2. What solid are they computing?
Is the Manim frame a proof of the formula or a picture of the limit? What additional step makes it a proof?
evaluate.hint: Take the limit of the Riemann sum.

create: Choose another region with a hole and predict which method has the simpler integral before calculating.
Use the Steinmetz result to compute the volume of the solid for r = 2 and check against the sum of square slabs.

checks.q: What is the difference between a washer and a shell?
checks.answer: A washer is perpendicular to the axis, a shell is a tube around it.

checks.q: Shell: rho = 2, h = 3, d rho = 0.1. Volume?
Why does the error fall when slices thin?
checks.answer: Each piece approximates the true volume element better; the error of a midpoint sum falls like 1/n^2.

checks.q: Both methods agree to 4 digits at 128 slices. Is it proof of correctness?
checks.answer: It strongly suggests correctness unless both share the same mistake (for example the wrong axis); compare with an independent formula like Pappus.

checks.q: Make up a region whose shell integral is trivial but whose washer integral needs a root.
checks.answer: A region under y = x^2 about the y-axis: shells give 2 pi x * x^2; washers need x = sqrt(y).
